input.quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: Compliant, at or above the fallback; no redline proposed. § 4(c) (p0021) is the sole grant of Contractor background material and it meets the rule's core material terms: it is royalty-free, non-exclusive and perpetual, it is nowhere described as revocable, and nothing in the agreement (including the § 6 termination provisions, p0032-p0033) lets RadialSpark revoke or terminate it at will, so the walk-away trigger of a discretionary revocation is absent. On the affiliates element, the clause does not use the word "Affiliates" - it addresses the same point through a phrasing variant: the grant expressly includes "the right to grant a sublicense," unconditional and not subject to consent or notice, which gives Clear Capital a self-executing path to extend the licence to its affiliates and to contractors acting on its behalf. That defeats the walk-away trigger of "affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them" and is at least as good as the fallback position, which would cover affiliates only on written notice. Use scope is also broad ("in connection with Company's business operations") rather than narrowed to internal use. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than redlined, per the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements: (i) the grant is not labelled "irrevocable," though perpetuity plus the absence of any revocation mechanic reaches the same practical result; and (ii) successor transfer is not addressed in the grant and falls to the mutual § 10 nonassignability clause (p0042), where consent "will not be unreasonably withheld" - a standard under which an M&A successor transfer should not be refusable. Company is Clear Capital and Contractor is RadialSpark, so the grant runs in our favour and should not be flagged.
